name: Orange-fronted Barbet
rangeDescription: Far southwestern colombia (southeastern nariño) and western ecuador (south to el oro)
description: Chunky black and white bird with a stout bill. Ranges in lowland and foothill rainforest west of the Andes in Ecuador and far southwestern Colombia.

name: Bronze-tailed Thornbill
rangeDescription: Páramo of northeastern colombia to far western venezuela
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with a rather large tail. Males and females are dingy greenish-olive overall.

name: Pygmy Tit
rangeDescription: Mountains of western and central java
description: Absolutely tiny round gray bird, comparable in size to a flowerpecker or small sunbird. Fairly plain overall, but note pale eyes, whitish underparts, and stout dark bill.

name: Western Bonelli's Warbler
rangeDescription: Western and central europe; winters to sahel of northern africa
description: Small, sleek warbler; white belly contrasts with olive and green upperparts. Very difficult to separate from Eastern Bonelli’s of Eastern Europe.

name: Spot-tailed Goshawk
rangeDescription: Sulawesi region, including talisei (to northeast), muna and buton (to southeast)
description: A small pale hawk restricted to Sulawesi and nearby islands. Adult has a pale gray head, a bright yellow mark between bill and eye, and conspicuous white tail spots.

name: Rufous-throated Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of western colombia and western ecuador (southward to el oro)
description: Distinctive small tanager with mostly black head, orange throat, and bold black spotting on underparts. Upperparts are dark with a scaled look.

name: Fork-tailed Pygmy-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil (rio de janeiro, southern minas gerais, and northeastern são paulo)
description: Tiny flycatcher with a very distinctive head pattern and tail. Best field marks are the cinnamon head and the long, forked white-tipped tail framed by a dark border.

name: Reunion White-eye
rangeDescription: Forest of réunion (western mascarene islands)
description: An unusual white-eye with dark plumage and a long, curved bill. Olive-green above and gray below with a broad white eye-ring.

name: Plain Sunbird
rangeDescription: Southern myanmar to malaya, sumatra including nias, borneo, and north natuna islands
description: A medium-large sunbird with a rather thick, slightly decurved bill. Extremely plain: pale olive-yellow above and paler washed-out yellow below.

name: Bertram's Weaver
rangeDescription: Highlands of tanzania, zambia, malawi, and northern mozambique
description: Fairly large, chunky weaver. Both sexes have a pale eye, an olive back, and yellow underparts.

name: Bali Myna
rangeDescription: Coastal northwestern bali (bali barat national park); extinct in the wild with reintroductions in nusa penida island and (usually unsuccessful) in western bali
description: An eye-catching white starling with black tips to the tail and wings, bare blue facial skin, and long plumes that hang down the nape. Juvenile is shorter-crested than adult, with yellow wash.

name: Burmese Nuthatch
rangeDescription: Myanmar to southeastern yunnan, thailand, laos, cambodia, and southern vietnam
description: Gray with a slender black mask and warm underparts. Male has white extending from the throat onto the cheeks, and averages darker below than the female, which also lacks the male’s white cheek patch.

name: Cinnamon-chested Bee-eater
rangeDescription: Highland forest of eastern africa
description: Colorful, medium-sized bee-eater with rich rufous underparts. In flight, shows black patches at the back of the wings and sides of the tail.

name: Monteiro's Hornbill
rangeDescription: Arid savanna of southern angola and northern namibia
description: Brown hornbill with a white belly and a yellow-and-orange bill. The white outer tail feathers and wing patches are conspicuous in flight.

name: Flying Steamer-Duck
rangeDescription: Southern chile (north to maule) and southern argentina (north to neuquén and southern buenos aires provinces)
description: A large, heavily built duck that is fairly common along rocky seacoasts and on lakes near the coast; also local and uncommon on larger lakes farther inland. Despite the name, rarely seen in flight; more often seen thrashing through the water like an old paddle steamer boat, hence the name.

name: Red-legged Cormorant
rangeDescription: Coastal peru and chile; isolated population in southern argentina
description: Attractive coastal cormorant; locally fairly common in Humboldt Current. Often seen perched on jetties, inshore rocks, and cliffs associating readily with Guanay Cormorant, pelicans, boobies, and Inca Terns.

name: Wire-crested Thorntail
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to eastern ecuador and northeastern peru
description: Small, compact hummingbird found on the east slope of Andes from central Colombia to central Peru. Male is unmistakable; look for long pointed tail, wirelike crest, short straight bill, and white band across the rump.

name: Mato Grosso Antbird
rangeDescription: Eastern bolivia to south-central brazil (mato grosso) and northern paraguay
description: Medium-sized antbird with a long graduated tail. Males are black with a white-tipped tail and wing coverts.

name: Maasai Apalis
rangeDescription: Maasai mara, southwestern kenya, and serengeti, northern tanzania
description: A slender ash-gray apalis with a diagnostic striking white panel on the folded wing and two pairs of white outer tail feathers which are usually obvious on the dark tail. Upperparts are darker than underparts.

name: Wangi-wangi White-eye
rangeDescription: Wangi-wangi, wakatobi (tukangbesi) islands, off southeastern sulawesi
description: Only described in 2022; endemic to the island of Wangi-Wangi in the Tukangbesi archipelago off the southeastern tip of Sulawesi. Relatively large and lanky for a white-eye, with a striking orangey-yellow bill immediately distinguishing it from Wakatobi White-eye, the only other white-eye on the island.
